title: Password Strength Classification

scenario.context: Evaluate five fictional passwords and identify the most resilient choice against modern hash cracking and brute force attacks.

options.text: Password123! — Has uppercase, numbers, and special character
admin2024 — Relevant and easy to remember
correct-horse-battery-staple-99 — Long multi-word passphrase with high entropy (40+ bits)
qwertyuiop — Easy keyboard pattern

indicators.description: Passphrase length (31 chars) provides exponential cryptographic entropy
Avoids predictable dictionary substitutions like P@ssw0rd
Estimated brute force crack time exceeds hundreds of thousands of centuries

explanation: Length trumps complexity! Long multi-word passphrases (like 'correct-horse-battery-staple-99') are exponentially harder for GPUs to brute-force than short complex passwords like 'Password123!', which are indexed in precomputed cracking wordlists (rockyou.txt).
hints: Which password has the longest total character count?
Why is 'Password123!' easily cracked despite having special characters?
Consider the mathematical power of four unrelated random words.
learningObjective: Understand why long passphrases with high entropy outperform short complex passwords.
consequenceChain: You chose a short predictable password like 'Password123!'
Attacker ran dictionary wordlist attack against password hash
Password cracked in under 0.04 seconds using standard GPU
recoverySteps: Migrate to a 4+ word random passphrase or dedicated password manager
Audit all accounts for common dictionary passwords
Check HaveIBeenPwned for known breach compromises

title: Password Reuse Risk Assessment

scenario.context: A fictional online fitness blog was breached in 2023, leaking 100,000 user emails and plaintext passwords. A user used 'SunsetBeach#2022' for both the fitness blog and their primary email account.

options.text: SAFE — The password is long and complex enough to stay secure
LOW RISK — Only the fitness blog is compromised, other sites are protected by their own firewalls
CRITICAL RISK — Attacker will execute Credential Stuffing to unlock email and bank accounts

indicators.description: Automated bots will test the leaked combination across thousands of websites
A single low-security site breach compromises high-value email and banking access
Reusing identical credentials creates a single point of failure

explanation: Password reuse exposes you to Credential Stuffing attacks. When an obscure or low-security website is breached, attackers use automated botnets to try those exact email/password pairs across major banks, email providers, and social platforms.
hints: What do automated attackers do immediately after acquiring a leaked database?
Why is primary email account compromise especially dangerous?
How does using unique passwords limit the blast radius of a breach?
learningObjective: Recognize the dangers of password reuse and understand credential stuffing attacks.
consequenceChain: Fitness forum database leaked onto darknet marketplace
Credential stuffing bot tested your email/password on primary mailbox
Attacker requested password resets on all connected banking and commerce accounts
recoverySteps: Immediately change passwords on all accounts sharing the breached credential
Use a password manager to generate unique, random 16+ character passwords for every service
Enable hardware or authenticator app 2FA on primary email and banking

title: Evaluating Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Methods

scenario.context: Select the MOST secure multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanism to protect against SIM-swapping, phishing proxies, and automated interception.

options.text: SMS Text Message (OTP) — Convenient 6-digit code sent to your mobile phone number
Email Verification Code — 6-digit PIN sent to your secondary mailbox
FIDO2 / WebAuthn Hardware Security Key (e.g., YubiKey) — Phishing-resistant cryptographic handshake
Security Questions (e.g., Mother's maiden name, childhood pet)

indicators.description: FIDO2 / WebAuthn is cryptographically bound to the genuine origin domain
Immune to SIM swapping and mobile carrier hijacking
Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) phishing proxies cannot relay WebAuthn challenge signatures

explanation: FIDO2 / WebAuthn hardware keys and Passkeys are the gold standard because they are mathematically bound to the browser's exact URL origin. SMS OTPs are vulnerable to SIM swaps and AitM phishing, while security questions can be researched via public records and social media.
hints: Which method binds the cryptographic signature directly to the true website domain?
Why is SMS authentication vulnerable to mobile carrier social engineering?
Can a phishing website trick a physical FIDO2 key?
learningObjective: Differentiate between MFA types and understand why FIDO2/WebAuthn provides phishing resistance.
consequenceChain: Attacker socially engineered mobile telecom agent to swap your SIM card
SMS OTP codes routed to attacker's phone handset
Attacker bypassed 2FA and took over cryptocurrency wallet
recoverySteps: Set a carrier port-out PIN password with your mobile provider
Switch critical accounts from SMS 2FA to authenticator apps or FIDO2 keys
Review account recovery phone numbers

title: Spotting Predictable Pattern Substitutions

scenario.context: An employee creates their corporate password using standard company patterns: CompanyName + Year + SpecialChar. Example: 'AcmeCorp2024!'. How vulnerable is this practice?

options.text: SECURE — It meets all complexity requirements (uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol)
VULNERABLE — Password cracking tools (Hashcat/John the Ripper) specifically target Season+Year+Symbol rule masks
MODERATE — Safe as long as the year changes every quarter

indicators.description: Password cracking tools run specialized rule-based masks for SeasonYearSymbol patterns
Attackers test 'SeasonYear!' against thousands of user accounts simultaneously (Password Spraying)

explanation: Season/Year/Symbol patterns (like 'Spring2024!') are the #1 target in corporate Password Spray attacks. Attackers try 'Spring2024!' across 50,000 corporate usernames without triggering individual account lockout thresholds.
hints: What is a Password Spraying attack?
Do password cracking tools use masks matching seasonal names?
Why does meeting arbitrary complexity rules not guarantee high entropy?
learningObjective: Recognize why formulaic passwords (Season+Year+Symbol) fall victim to password spraying.
consequenceChain: Attacker launched password spray attack trying 'Autumn2024!' across the corporate directory
35 employee accounts with identical patterns compromised simultaneously
Attacker established persistence without tripping account lockouts
recoverySteps: Implement Azure AD / Entra ID Password Protection to ban predictable patterns
Enforce minimum 16-character passphrases over arbitrary complexity rules
Mandate MFA challenge on every external corporate login

title: Password Manager Master Key Hygiene

scenario.context: You configure a dedicated Password Manager to store 250 unique website credentials. Which strategy is recommended for your Master Password and Recovery Key?

options.text: Store the master password in a notes app on your phone for easy access
Use a memorable 5-word Diceware passphrase, store encrypted emergency sheet in a physical safe, and enforce biometric + 2FA
Use your standard social media password so you never forget it
Email the master key to your personal Gmail account as a backup

indicators.description: 5-word Diceware passphrase offers ~65 bits of true cryptographic entropy
Physical offline emergency recovery kit protects against cloud lockout
Ensures zero-knowledge end-to-end encryption cannot be decrypted by vendor

explanation: The master password is the single vault key for your entire digital life. It must be generated using high-entropy methods (e.g. 5+ random Diceware words), never stored in unencrypted digital notes or cloud docs, and backed up on physical emergency kits in a secure offline location.
hints: Why is saving passwords in plain text notes or cloud storage dangerous?
What is Diceware passphrase generation?
Where should recovery emergency kits be physically stored?
learningObjective: Master password vault security, Diceware passphrase generation, and offline key management.
consequenceChain: Master password was saved in an unencrypted cloud notes app
Notes app account compromised through third-party data leak
Attacker decrypted entire password vault containing all 250 stored credentials
recoverySteps: Assume all 250 accounts in vault are compromised and rotate all passwords immediately
Generate new vault with 5-word Diceware master passphrase
Store emergency access kit only in physical fireproof safe

title: Passkeys vs Traditional Passwords

scenario.context: Modern web applications offer 'Passkeys' (based on FIDO2/WebAuthn public key cryptography). How do Passkeys fundamentally improve user security compared to traditional passwords?

options.text: Passkeys are just 30-character random passwords that get auto-filled by Google Chrome
Passkeys use public-key cryptography where the server only stores a public key, making server data breaches harmless to your credentials
Passkeys eliminate the need for device screen locks or biometrics
Passkeys only work on desktop computers with USB ports

indicators.description: Private key never leaves the secure enclave of your user device
Server only holds public key; database breach reveals no secrets
Browser will not sign challenge unless domain origin matches exactly

explanation: Passkeys replace shared secrets with asymmetric public-key cryptography. The server stores only a public key. Even if the server's database is completely breached by hackers, there are no passwords or secrets to steal!
hints: What is the difference between symmetric shared secrets and public key cryptography?
Can an attacker use a public key to impersonate you?
Why are Passkeys impossible to phish on a fake domain?
learningObjective: Understand Passkey architecture, asymmetric authentication, and database breach resilience.
consequenceChain: Web service was breached and hacker dumped database of password hashes
Because you used traditional password, attackers queued hash for GPU cracking
Passkey users remained completely unharmed because only public keys were stored
recoverySteps: Enable Passkeys on supporting accounts (Google, Apple, Microsoft, GitHub, Amazon)
Sync Passkeys securely via encrypted ecosystems (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager, 1Password)
Maintain at least one backup hardware security key

title: Session Hijacking via Stolen Browser Cookies

scenario.context: You log into an account using a strong 20-character password and 2FA. You check 'Remember Me on this PC'. A malicious browser extension steals your active session cookie. Can the attacker access your account without your password or 2FA?

options.text: NO — The attacker still needs to enter your password and MFA code
YES — The session cookie represents an already-authenticated state, bypassing password and MFA checks completely
NO — Cookies only store visual website themes and layout preferences

indicators.description: Session tokens bypass authentication barriers because identity has already been validated
Infostealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar) extract SQLite cookie databases from browser profiles

explanation: Session Hijacking (Pass-the-Cookie) bypasses passwords and MFA. Once logged in, the server gives your browser a session cookie (e.g. 'session_id=xyz'). If malware or an extension steals that token, the attacker injects it into their browser and is instantly logged in as you.
hints: What is the purpose of an authentication session cookie?
Does the server ask for MFA on every single web page request, or does it check the session cookie?
Why is malware that steals browser cookies so dangerous?
learningObjective: Understand session token hijacking and why endpoint hygiene matters even with MFA enabled.
consequenceChain: Malicious browser extension copied browser session storage and cookies
Attacker loaded cookie into anti-detect browser and accessed mailbox
No MFA prompt was triggered because the session was already verified
recoverySteps: Click 'Log out of all devices / Revoke all sessions' in account security settings
Audit and remove untrusted browser extensions
Enable device-bound session credentials (DBSC) where available

title: Defending Against Social Engineering Password Resets

scenario.context: Attackers frequently target 'Forgot Password' recovery flows rather than cracking the actual password. Which defense configuration best secures your account recovery workflow?

options.text: Use easily remembered security questions about your high school mascot and hometown
Use fictional random passphrases for security questions, disable SMS recovery, and require hardware-backed recovery codes
Leave recovery options unconfigured so no one can reset it
Link account recovery to a public social media profile

indicators.description: Prevents OSINT reconnaissance from answering security questions
Ensures the weakest recovery link does not undermine strong master credentials

explanation: Account recovery is often the weakest link in authentication. If your security question is 'What city were you born in?', an attacker can find the answer in 2 minutes on public genealogical records or social media. Treat security questions like extra passwords and answer with random passphrases.
hints: Can attackers discover your pet's name or mother's maiden name using public OSINT?
Do security questions need to contain truthful answers?
Why must recovery paths be as secure as primary login paths?
learningObjective: Harden account recovery mechanisms against OSINT reconnaissance and social engineering resets.
consequenceChain: Attacker researched your mother's maiden name from public family social media post
Submitted password reset request and answered security questions correctly
Overrode your 20-character password and locked you out of the account
recoverySteps: Store fake/random answers to security questions inside your password manager
Remove SMS recovery fallback on critical accounts
Download and store offline 16-character backup recovery codes in a physical safe
